clips.file: Person in red top near a red car.mp4
clips.directive: Find a person wearing a red top
must: A person wearing a red top is visible walking in the car park.
The person walks toward the red car, getting closer to it.
The person reaches the red car.
The account ends with the person getting into the red car, stated plainly.
must_not: The person walks away from the red car or moves farther from it.
The red car arrives, drives in, enters the frame, or moves (it is parked and stationary throughout).
The person's entering the car is hedged as only possible or suggested (for example 'possibly', 'appears to have', 'suggesting they entered').
The person is called a child or lost, or is given an age, identity or motive.
A vehicle is named by make or model (for example Volkswagen or Tiguan) instead of by colour and type.
The account ends with the person merely standing beside the car with no mention that they are no longer visible or got in.
The narration mentions tracking, software, detection, measurements, tiles, sheets, frames or images instead of describing the footage itself.

clips.file: car with open doors in parking.mp4
must: A silver or grey SUV or similar car in the car park is reported as having doors open.
More than one open door is mentioned, or the driver's side door and a rear door.
The car is reported as matching the request to find cars with open doors.
must_not: A person is said to be visible in, beside or getting out of the car (no person is visible).
The narration says the doors were opened for a reason or calls the car stolen, suspicious or a threat. Saying the car is unattended is fine.
The other parked cars are said to have open doors.
A vehicle is named by make or model stated as fact (without 'appears to be' or 'looks like') when no logo or badge is legible.
The narration mentions tracking, software, detection, measurements, tiles, sheets, frames or images instead of describing the footage itself.

must: A dark or black backpack is on a wooden bench.
No person is visible near the backpack at any point; it is left alone.
The backpack is reported as matching the request to find unattended bags or items.
must_not: A person is said to be visible, sitting on the bench, or walking away from it.
The backpack is called dangerous, suspicious or a threat, or given an owner or reason for being there.
The backpack is said to move or to be picked up.
The narration mentions tracking, software, detection, measurements, tiles, sheets, frames or images instead of describing the footage itself.
